column1: # The reference parser's canonical value for each document in
# tests/json-value/corpus, pinned.  One row per document, six tab-separated
# columns: path, verdict (accept|refuse), value, class, offset, sha256.
# value is the lowercase hex of the UTF-8 bytes of renderValue (canonValue v),
# where v = decodeTape (parseBytes Limits.default doc); '-' on a refusal.
# class and offset are parseErrorName's and parseErrorOffset's, '-' where the
# row does not carry one.  sha256 is the document's digest.
# rendering: LeanLLVM.JSON.renderValue (LeanLLVM.Refinement.canonValue v)
# refusals: LeanLLVM.Refinement.parseErrorName / parseErrorOffset
# The value rows are the values at 47a2096, measured against the committed
# JsonMain.renderValue -- the definition the value arm relocates to
# LeanLLVM.JSON.Render.  The class/offset rows are the working-tree relocation
# of the refusal renderers (JsonPipelineSpec.lean, uncommitted), whose
# vocabulary is invalid:<Reject constructor> with the constructor's position,
# and '-' where the reject carries none.  The relocation must print these rows
# byte for byte; a differing row is a changed printer, not a stale table.
# Limit outcomes (depthExceeded, inputTooLong, outOfCapacity) are waived: each
# needs an input far past a corpus document's size, and the byte-order-mark row
# exercises the same parseErrorOffset -> none path that the limits' rows would.
